headline: Scalable inference methods target phylogenies, viral fitness and haplotypes
label: Probabilistic Inference For Phylogenetics
summary: Low-coverage single-cell, long-read and large heterogeneous datasets motivate new scalable inference methods for phylogenies and viral genomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is probabilistic inference of evolutionary and genomic structure from sequence data under explicit models. Conditional generative models trained with discrete diffusion over phylogenetic trees recover MCMC posteriors more accurately than Phyloformer 2 on the reported datasets, while adaptive minibatch SMC-ABC cuts the cost of mechanistic inference on large heterogeneous biological data by growing batches as posteriors refine. Two items address haplotype resolution: virCHap phases viral haplotypes from long reads using graph partitioning, and SLAFIT reconstructs haplotypes from third-generation reads to infer linkage-aware viral fitness and structural variants. A tumor phylogeny study shows that bin size critically affects copy-number-based inference from low-coverage single-cell DNA-seq. The novelty lies in scalable or read-level methods extending inference to more complex processes and sparser data.
